content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad made with a light mayonnaise-type dressing originated in 1958. It is a classic dish where hard‑boiled eggs are mixed with a delicate, lower‑fat mayo, sometimes flavored with mustard, dill, and green onions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe became popular in post‑war America as a quick, inexpensive meal.
Light mayonnaise was developed in the 1950s as a lower‑calorie alternative to traditional mayo.
The salad is often served as a sandwich filling, on salad plates, or as a picnic snack.
The original version used only yolks, vinegar, and oil, without egg whites.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin, and folate, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: Light mayonnaise contains fewer fats and calories than regular mayo, making the salad more diet‑friendly.

items.title: Source of choline
items.content: Choline in yolks is important for liver health and cognitive function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in yolks help protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Yolks are high in cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella; ensure eggs are fully cooked.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Light mayonnaise often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the egg salad cold as a snack, in sandwiches, on lettuce leaves, or as a filling for stuffed vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs, paprika, or finely diced cucumber.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off odor or discoloration.
